answer: Each agent registers a cryptographic vault recording a payment source, timestamps and a shared secret; the network then clusters any identities whose vaults share these attributes into one kin‑linked node. On a terrace of the consensus, a karst‑hardness score is computed: intersecting flows lower trust and trigger a fable‑like ban of the linked group. An attacker must generate independent payment channels, unique timestamps and secrets for every fake node, making the cost grow linearly with the Sybil count.
